title: Persuading
job: Make a case, concede a point, hold your ground
verifiedBy: Claude Opus 5 — LLM review, authorised by repo owner

allowedPatterns: min nāḥiya + <clause> + , + wa min nāḥiya ukhrā + <clause>

rules.text: raghma anna is one of ʾanna's sisters, like L3-M3's anna and L1-M9's li-ʾanna: it holds a whole CLAUSE, and the noun after it is accusative — a case this course does not write.
ʿalā ar-raghm min holds a NOUN or L3-M1's maṣdar, never a clause. It is the same clause-against-noun split L4-M2 drew between li-ʾanna and bi-sabab, and it is decided by shape, never by feel.
wa maʿa dhālika answers the concession. Arabic is happy to mark BOTH halves — raghma anna in front, wa maʿa dhālika behind — where English allows only one and calls the other a fault.
bal CORRECTS: it replaces the thing just denied, so it requires a negative in front of it. laysa X bal Y. English has no single word for it and reaches for two, but rather.
English picks although, despite and but by feel, and forbids marking both halves of a concession. Arabic picks by the shape of what follows, and expects both halves marked.
lākin and bal are not interchangeable. lākin ADDS a contrasting fact to something you have let stand; bal REPLACES something you have just denied, and cannot appear without that denial.
lā shakka anna and min al-wāḍiḥ anna are frozen assertion frames. They keep the vowels this course otherwise drops, exactly as as-salāmu ʿalaykum and L2-M1's lā baʾsa do.
min nāḥiya … wa min nāḥiya ukhrā lays two sides of a question flat. It is a frame rather than vocabulary: the second half points back at a first half that has to be there.
ghayr negates a NOUN or an adjective where lā negates a verb: ghayr ṣaḥīḥ not correct, ghayr muhimm unimportant. lā in front of an adjective is not Arabic.

sentences.display: raghma anna al-lugha ṣaʿba, adrus kull yawm
sentences.script: رغم أن اللغة صعبة، أدرس كل يوم
sentences.cue: Although the language is hard, I study every day
sentences.literal: Despite that the-language hard, I-study every day

words.note: Another of ʾanna's sisters (L3-M3): it holds a whole clause, and the noun straight after it is accusative — a case this course does not write.

sentences.trap: English lets although take a noun — although the difficulty. Arabic will not: raghma anna needs a clause with a subject and a predicate behind it, and a bare noun takes the other frame.
sentences.sound: RAGH-ma AN-na: the gh is the gargled r at the back of the throat, and anna's doubled n is held.

variations.display: raghma anna aṭ-ṭaqs bārid, adhhab ilā al-ʿamal
variations.script: رغم أن الطقس بارد، أذهب إلى العمل
variations.cue: Although the weather is cold, I go to work
variations.changed: the concession: a hard language → cold weather

variations.display: raghma anna al-mudīr ghāḍib, al-ʿamal jayyid
variations.script: رغم أن المدير غاضب، العمل جيد
variations.cue: Although the manager is angry, the work is good
variations.changed: both halves: studying → a verdict with no verb in it

mistake.why: raghma anna wants a clause. With a bare noun the frame has to be ʿalā ar-raghm min, and the two are not interchangeable.

sentences.usage: Granting a difficulty before you say what you do anyway — the opening move of an argument.
sentences.mnemonic: raghma anna takes a clause; the noun waits for ʿalā ar-raghm min.

sentences.display: ʿalā ar-raghm min al-maṭar, dhahabtu ilā as-sūq
sentences.script: على الرغم من المطر، ذهبت إلى السوق
sentences.cue: Despite the rain, I went to the market
sentences.literal: On the-despite from the-rain, I-went to the-market

words.note: The noun half of the pair. It takes a noun or L3-M1's maṣdar and never a clause — the same split L4-M2 drew between bi-sabab and li-ʾanna.

sentences.trap: English chooses despite over although by feel. Arabic chooses by shape: a clause takes raghma anna, a noun takes ʿalā ar-raghm min, and swapping them is a broken sentence rather than a style slip.
sentences.sound: ʿa-lā ar-RAGH-mi min — said as one run, with the article's r doubled onto the end of ʿalā.

variations.display: ʿalā ar-raghm min al-izdiḥām, waṣaltu mubakkiran
variations.script: على الرغم من الازدحام، وصلت مبكراً
variations.cue: Despite the traffic, I arrived early
variations.changed: the obstacle: rain → traffic

variations.display: ʿalā ar-raghm min at-taʾakhkhur, al-ijtimāʿ jayyid
variations.script: على الرغم من التأخر، الاجتماع جيد
variations.cue: Despite the delay, the meeting is good
variations.changed: a maṣdar behind min — L3-M1's noun-from-a-verb doing the work a clause would do

mistake.display: ʿalā ar-raghm min al-maṭar nazala, dhahabtu ilā as-sūq
mistake.script: على الرغم من المطر نزل، ذهبت إلى السوق
mistake.why: A clause cannot follow min. The moment there is a verb inside the concession, the frame has to become raghma anna.

sentences.usage: Naming the obstacle you got past, in one noun, before you say what you did.
sentences.mnemonic: min takes a noun — it always has.

sentences.display: al-fikra jayyida, wa maʿa dhālika lastu muwāfiq
sentences.script: الفكرة جيدة، ومع ذلك لست موافق
sentences.cue: The idea is good, and even so I don't agree
sentences.literal: The-idea good, and with that not-I agreeing

words.note: Literally with that. It answers a concession, and it wants the wa in front of it: wa maʿa dhālika is the frame, maʿa dhālika alone is a preposition.

sentences.trap: English forbids although … but inside one sentence. Arabic expects the answering half to be marked, so raghma anna … wa maʿa dhālika is the ordinary shape rather than a doubling.
sentences.sound: MA-ʿa DHĀ-li-ka: the ʿayn in maʿa is the throat sound, and dhālika opens with the dh of this.

variations.display: al-fikra jayyida, wa maʿa dhālika al-waqt qaṣīr
variations.script: الفكرة جيدة، ومع ذلك الوقت قصير
variations.cue: The idea is good, and even so there isn't time
variations.changed: the objection: I don't agree → there isn't time

variations.display: al-ʿamal ṣaʿb, wa maʿa dhālika anā saʿīd
variations.script: العمل صعب، ومع ذلك أنا سعيد
variations.cue: The work is hard, and even so I'm happy
variations.changed: both halves: an idea and agreeing → work and being happy

mistake.display: al-fikra jayyida, maʿa dhālika lastu muwāfiq
mistake.script: الفكرة جيدة، مع ذلك لست موافق
mistake.why: Without the wa the phrase reads as the plain preposition with that, and the sentence loses the join that made it a concession.

sentences.usage: Conceding the other side's point and refusing it in the same breath.
sentences.mnemonic: Both halves marked: raghma anna in front, wa maʿa dhālika behind.

sentences.display: laysat al-mushkila fī al-waqt, bal fī at-tarkīz
sentences.script: ليست المشكلة في الوقت، بل في التركيز
sentences.cue: The problem isn't the time, it's the concentration
sentences.literal: Not-is the-problem in the-time, but-rather in the-concentration

words.note: It REPLACES what was just denied, so it needs a negative in front of it. English has no single word for it and reaches for but, which only adds.
A maṣdar of the L3-M1 kind — the act of focusing, used here as an ordinary noun. The sun-letter t doubles onto the article: written al-, said at-tarkīz.

sentences.trap: English but does two jobs: adding a contrast and correcting a denial. Arabic splits them — lākin adds, bal corrects — and bal with no negative in front of it is not a sentence.
sentences.sound: bal — one short syllable, said hard against the pause before it.

variations.display: laysat al-mushkila fī al-mudīr, bal fī al-ʿamal
variations.script: ليست المشكلة في المدير، بل في العمل
variations.cue: The problem isn't the manager, it's the work
variations.changed: what is denied and what replaces it

variations.display: laysa al-kitāb ghālī, bal rakhīṣ
variations.script: ليس الكتاب غالي، بل رخيص
variations.cue: The book isn't expensive, it's cheap
variations.changed: the shape of the two halves: prepositional phrases → a bare adjective

mistake.display: al-mushkila fī al-waqt, bal fī at-tarkīz
mistake.script: المشكلة في الوقت، بل في التركيز
mistake.why: bal has nothing to correct. Without laysat in front of it there is no denial for bal to replace, and the sentence contradicts itself.

sentences.usage: Correcting somebody's diagnosis without calling them wrong — the most useful single word in the level.

sentences.display: lā shakka anna al-ʿamal muhimm jiddan
sentences.script: لا شك أن العمل مهم جدًا
sentences.cue: There's no doubt that the work is very important
sentences.literal: No doubt that the-work important very

words.note: Frozen with its -a, the way L2-M1's lā baʾsa is. Another of ʾanna's sisters, and the clause behind it is an ordinary one.

sentences.trap: English softens an assertion almost by reflex — I'm pretty sure. This module does not: the frame states the thing flatly, and every hedge belongs to the module after it.
sentences.sound: lā SHAK-ka AN-na: two doubled consonants in a row, both of them held.

variations.display: lā shakka anna al-lugha ṣaʿba
variations.script: لا شك أن اللغة صعبة
variations.cue: There's no doubt the language is hard
variations.changed: what is being asserted

variations.display: lā shakka anna al-mudīr ghāḍib
variations.script: لا شك أن المدير غاضب
variations.cue: There's no doubt the manager is angry
variations.changed: the clause behind the frame

mistake.display: lā shakk anna al-ʿamal muhimm jiddan
mistake.script: لا شك أن العمل مهم جدًا
mistake.why: The phrase is frozen as lā shakka, with the -a its own grammar put there, exactly as lā baʾsa is. Dropping the vowel leaves half a phrase.

sentences.usage: Opening the half of an argument you are not conceding.
sentences.mnemonic: lā shakka anna — no doubt, then the clause.

sentences.display: min al-wāḍiḥ anna as-siʿr ghālī jiddan
sentences.script: من الواضح أن السعر غالي جدًا
sentences.cue: It's obvious that the price is very expensive
sentences.literal: From the-clear that the-price expensive very

words.note: Literally from the clear. Arabic builds its impersonal openers out of min plus an adjective with the article on it, and ʾanna carries the clause as always.
Masculine. The sun-letter s doubles onto the article: written al-, said as-siʿr. The plural is asʿār.

sentences.trap: English needs a dummy subject — it's obvious that. Arabic has no dummy subject at all: min al-wāḍiḥ is a phrase standing where a subject would be, and nothing in it agrees with anything.
sentences.sound: min al-WĀ-ḍiḥ AN-na — the ḍ is the heavy d, said with the tongue flat against the roof of the mouth.

variations.display: min al-wāḍiḥ anna al-mudīr mashghūl
variations.script: من الواضح أن المدير مشغول
variations.cue: It's obvious the manager is busy
variations.changed: the clause behind the frame

variations.display: min al-wāḍiḥ anna as-siʿr rakhīṣ
variations.script: من الواضح أن السعر رخيص
variations.cue: It's obvious the price is cheap
variations.changed: the verdict on the price: expensive → cheap

mistake.display: min wāḍiḥ anna as-siʿr ghālī jiddan
mistake.script: من واضح أن السعر غالي جدًا
mistake.why: The adjective carries the article here: al-wāḍiḥ. Without it the phrase is not the impersonal opener but a stray from-clear.

sentences.usage: Asserting a shared fact you expect no argument about, before the part you do expect argument about.
sentences.mnemonic: min + the adjective + anna: from the clear that …

sentences.display: min nāḥiya al-bayt kabīr, wa min nāḥiya ukhrā al-ījār ghālī
sentences.script: من ناحية البيت كبير، ومن ناحية أخرى الإيجار غالي
sentences.cue: On one hand the house is big, on the other the rent is expensive
sentences.literal: From side the-house big, and from side other the-rent expensive

words.note: A side of a thing. min nāḥiya opens one side of a question, and the answering half is min nāḥiya ukhrā.
ukhrā is the feminine of other, agreeing with nāḥiya. The phrase is the second half of a frame and does not open a sentence on its own.

sentences.trap: English lets on the other hand stand alone. Arabic's pair is a frame: the second half points back at a first half that has to have been said.
sentences.sound: NĀ-ḥi-ya: the ḥ is the breathy h from the throat, not the ordinary one. UKH-rā ends on a long ā.

variations.display: min nāḥiya al-ʿamal jayyid, wa min nāḥiya ukhrā al-waqt qaṣīr
variations.script: من ناحية العمل جيد، ومن ناحية أخرى الوقت قصير
variations.cue: On one hand the work is good, on the other there isn't time
variations.changed: the two sides: a house and its rent → work and time

variations.display: min nāḥiya al-kitāb muhimm, wa min nāḥiya ukhrā as-siʿr ghālī
variations.script: من ناحية الكتاب مهم، ومن ناحية أخرى السعر غالي
variations.cue: On one hand the book matters, on the other the price is high
variations.changed: the two sides being weighed against each other

mistake.why: The second half alone has nothing to answer. The pair opens with min nāḥiya, and only then does ukhrā mean anything.

sentences.usage: Laying two sides of a decision out flat before you choose between them.
sentences.mnemonic: One side, then the other side: nāḥiya, nāḥiya ukhrā.

sentences.display: maʿaka ḥaqq, wa lākin al-waqt qaṣīr
sentences.cue: You have a point, but there isn't time
sentences.literal: With-you right, and but the-time short

words.note: Literally with you is right. L1's maʿaka carrying a noun instead of a person, and the ordinary way to grant a point before taking it back.

sentences.trap: English you're right puts the rightness on the person. Arabic puts it beside them — the right is with you — and nothing in the sentence agrees with anybody.
sentences.sound: MA-ʿa-ka ḤAQQ — the final qq is held, and the ḥ is the breathy one.

variations.display: maʿaki ḥaqq, wa lākin as-siʿr ghālī
variations.script: معكِ حق، ولكن السعر غالي
variations.cue: You have a point, but the price is high
variations.changed: who is being answered: a man → a woman, and the objection with them

variations.display: maʿaka ḥaqq, wa lākin lastu muwāfiq
variations.script: معكَ حق، ولكن لست موافق
variations.cue: You have a point, but I don't agree
variations.changed: the objection: no time → no agreement

mistake.display: anta ṣaḥīḥ, wa lākin al-waqt qaṣīr
mistake.why: ṣaḥīḥ describes a statement, not a person — anta ṣaḥīḥ calls somebody correct the way a sum is correct. For a person the phrase is maʿaka ḥaqq.

sentences.usage: Conceding in one breath so you can object in the next — the move this module exists for.
sentences.mnemonic: The right is WITH you: maʿaka ḥaqq.

words.note: L1-M2's bi- on the noun for frankness, written joined as every bi- is. It opens a sentence and warns that what follows is blunt.
It negates a NOUN or an adjective where lā negates a verb: ghayr ṣaḥīḥ not correct, ghayr muhimm unimportant.

sentences.trap: English negates an adjective with not, or with a prefix — incorrect. Arabic cannot put lā there at all: lā ṣaḥīḥ is not Arabic, and ghayr is the word that does the job.
sentences.sound: bi-ṣa-RĀ-ḥa: the ṣ is the heavy s. ghayr opens with the gargled gh and ends on a hard r.

variations.display: bi-ṣarāḥa, hādhā ghayr muhimm
variations.script: بصراحة، هذا غير مهم
variations.cue: Frankly, this isn't important
variations.changed: what is negated: correct → important

variations.display: bi-ṣarāḥa, al-fikra ghayr jayyida
variations.script: بصراحة، الفكرة غير جيدة
variations.cue: Frankly, the idea isn't good
variations.changed: the subject and the adjective, which is now feminine

mistake.why: lā negates verbs. In front of an adjective the word is ghayr, and lā ṣaḥīḥ reads as a refusal rather than a judgement.

sentences.usage: Flagging that you are about to be direct — which in this register is a courtesy, not an attack.
sentences.mnemonic: ghayr for a word, lā for a verb.

sentences.display: ʿalā kulli ḥāl, fī raʾyī al-fikra muhimma fiʿlan
sentences.script: على كل حال، في رأيي الفكرة مهمة فعلًا
sentences.cue: In any case, in my opinion the idea really does matter
sentences.literal: On every state, in opinion-my the-idea important really

words.note: Frozen with the vowels its own grammar put there, like as-salāmu ʿalaykum. It sets the concessions aside and closes the argument.
The adverbial -an of L2-M1's shukran and jazīlan, on the noun for a deed. It sits behind what it strengthens, where jiddan sits.

sentences.trap: English really slides almost anywhere in a sentence. fiʿlan is an adverb of the -an kind and takes the slot L1-M3's jiddan already taught you: behind the word it strengthens.
sentences.sound: ʿa-lā KUL-li ḤĀL — one run, no pause. FIʿ-lan: the ʿayn sits inside the word, between the f and the l.

variations.display: ʿalā kulli ḥāl, fī raʾyī al-fikra jayyida
variations.script: على كل حال، في رأيي الفكرة جيدة
variations.cue: In any case, in my opinion the idea is good
variations.changed: the verdict: it really matters → it is good

variations.display: ʿalā kulli ḥāl, sa-adhhab ghadan
variations.script: على كل حال، سأذهب غدًا
variations.cue: In any case, I'll go tomorrow
variations.changed: what survives the argument: an opinion → a decision

mistake.display: ʿalā kull ḥāl, fī raʾyī al-fikra muhimma fiʿlan
mistake.script: على كل حال، في رأيي الفكرة مهمة فعلًا
mistake.why: The phrase is frozen as ʿalā kulli ḥāl. This course drops case endings everywhere else and keeps them inside frozen phrases, which is exactly what this is.

sentences.usage: Closing: you have granted what you will grant, and this is the part you are not moving on.
sentences.mnemonic: In any case — kulli ḥāl, every state of affairs.
